left.title: Bureau of Prisons chief removed in wake of Jeffrey Epstein suicide
left.body: Washington (CNN)Attorney General William Barr removed the acting head of the Bureau of Prisons, the Justice Department said Monday, replacing the agency's top official in the wake of the suicide of Jeffrey Epstein earlier this month. In a statement, Barr said Hugh Hurwitz, who had served in the acting position since last year, would return to the assistant director position he formerly occupied. Dr. Kathleen Hawk Sawyer, who led the bureau from 1992 to 2003, will be the new director, Barr said.
left.roundup: Attorney General William Barr has ordered the removal of Bureau of Prisons chief, Hugh Hurwitz, a week after Jeffery Epstein committed suicide in his jail cell. Barr appointed former director of US prisons, Kathleen Hawk Sawyer, to her old position. Hawk Sawyer served as director from 1992 to 2003. Media outlets show no significant differences in reporting, as the news is breaking.

center.title: Attorney General Barr orders removal of acting US prisons director after Epstein’s death
center.body: Attorney General William Barr has ordered the removal of a top U.S. prisons official following Jeffrey Epstein’s death. In a statement Monday, the attorney general said he will name Kathleen Hawk Sawyer the new director of the Federal Bureau of Prisons. She will replace Hugh Hurwitz, the acting director of the agency that oversees inmates in federal prisons. Barr said he will appoint Thomas Kane as the deputy director of the prisons bureau. Meanwhile, Hurwitz will lead the agency’s Reentry Services Division, according to the attorney general.

right.title: Acting director for the Bureau of Prisons is FIRED one week after the suicide of Jeffrey Epstein in federal custody
right.body: The acting director of the federal Bureau of Prisons has been removed from his position more than a week after millionaire financier Jeffrey Epstein took his own life while in federal custody. Attorney General William Barr announced Hugh Hurwitz’s reassignment Monday. Hurwitz had served as the agency’s acting director since May 2018. No reason was given for the reassignment, but the move comes as the bureau faces increased scrutiny after Epstein’s suicide August 10 at a New York jail.
